title: Coordinate Geometry: Straight Lines and Circles
seo_title: Year 12 A Level Maths: Straight Lines and Circles Worksheets
standard_text: Understand and use the equation of a straight line, including the forms y − y₁ = m(x − x₁) and ax + by + c = 0; gradient conditions for parallel and perpendicular lines; the coordinate geometry of the circle, including (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² and completing the square to find the centre and radius.
meta_desc: Free Year 12 A level maths worksheets on coordinate geometry: gradients, equations of straight lines, equations of circles, centre and radius, and completing the square. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: A circle with centre (a, b) and radius r: (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r².
body_html:
How it works

Line through (x₁, y₁) with gradient m: y − y₁ = m(x − x₁). Parallel lines have equal gradients; perpendicular gradients satisfy m₁m₂ = −1.

A circle (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r² has centre (a, b) and radius r. Complete the square in x and y to find them.

Example

Centre and radius of x² + y² − 6x + 4y = 3.

(x − 3)² + (y + 2)² = 16

Answer: (3, −2), radius 4

Common mistakes

  • Giving the centre of (x − 3)² + … as (−3, …).
  • Using r² instead of r for the radius.
  • Using the negative of the gradient (not the negative reciprocal) for a perpendicular line.

faq.q: How do you find the centre and radius from x² + y² + … = 0?
faq.a: Complete the square for x and for y, then move the constants to the right-hand side to get (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r².

faq.q: How do you test if lines are perpendicular?
faq.a: Multiply their gradients. If the product is −1, they are perpendicular.

items.q: The endpoints of a diameter are (−2, 5) and (−4, 3). Write the equation of the circle.
